title: 6.10.5 Lab: Bounce
description: The ball moves by two speeds you control. Bounce it off three walls and the paddle, let the paddle steer it, and serve it again when it falls out.

steps.title: Move the ball
steps.instructions:
The starter has the finished paddle from 6.10.4 and a ball: a white circle 12 pixels wide, so its radius `R` is 6. It has `collider = 'none'`, so nothing pushes it, slows it or pulls it down: your code moves it, as with Defender's shots in 5.9.5. `vx` and `vy` hold its speed in pixels per frame: `vx` across (`+` is right) and `vy` down (`+` is down, `-` is up). `serve()` puts the ball at (200, 300) with `vx` 3 and `vy` -4, and `draw()` calls `moveBall()` every frame, which is empty. The words at the top show vx and vy.

In `moveBall()`, add `vx` to the ball's x and `vy` to its y. Run it: the ball flies up and to the right, and off the screen. Press Run again to bring it back.
hints: `+=` adds to what is there: `ball.x += vx` is `ball.x = ball.x + vx`.

steps.title: Bounce off three walls
steps.instructions: A bounce is a flipped sign: `vx = -vx` turns 3 into -3 (going left) and -3 back into 3. The ball's x is its centre, so its side touches the left wall when `ball.x` is `R`, not 0, and the right wall when it is `400 - R` (6.10.2). Under the two moving lines, add: if `ball.x` is less than `R` OR more than `400 - R`, flip `vx`. Then: if `ball.y` is less than `R` (the top), flip `vy`. There is no bottom wall. Run it: the ball bounces off the left, the right and the top, and falls out at the bottom.

steps.title: Off the paddle, and steer
steps.instructions: `ball.overlaps(paddle)` is true on every frame the two touch (5.9.5), so flip `vy` only while the ball is coming down: `if (ball.overlaps(paddle) && vy > 0) { ... }`. Inside, flip `vy`, then set `vx` from where the ball landed: `vx = (ball.x - paddle.x) / 10;`. `ball.x - paddle.x` is how far right of the paddle's centre the ball is, negative on the left half (the A-to-B subtraction of 6.8.8), so the left end sends the ball left and the right end sends it right. Run it and catch the ball on different parts of the paddle: watch `vx` change in the words.
hints: Two lines inside the `if`: `vy = -vy;` and then `vx = (ball.x - paddle.x) / 10;`.
Without `&& vy > 0`, a paddle sliding into the ball from the side can flip it again and again while they touch.

steps.title: A lost ball comes back
steps.instructions: The bottom is open. At the end of `moveBall()`, if the ball's y is more than `400 + R` (all of it below the bottom edge), call `serve()` to put it back. Run it, miss on purpose, and the ball comes back above the paddle.
hints: `serve()` is already written: it puts the ball back and resets vx and vy.

requirements.title: The ball moves by vx and vy
requirements.description: Every frame vx is added to the ball's x and vy to its y. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)

requirements.title: The side walls flip vx
requirements.description: When the ball is less than R from the left wall or more than 400 - R across, vx changes sign. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)

requirements.title: The top flips vy
requirements.description: When the ball is less than R from the top, vy changes sign. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)

requirements.title: The paddle bounces it only while it comes down
requirements.description: When the ball overlaps the paddle AND vy is above 0, vy changes sign. Help: 6.10.2 (Reading: A ball you move yourself)

requirements.title: Where it lands steers it
requirements.description: After a paddle bounce, vx is worked out from the ball's x minus the paddle's x. Help: 6.10.3 (Worked Example: A ball in a box)

requirements.title: A lost ball is served again
requirements.description: When the ball's y is past the bottom, serve() puts it back. Help: 6.10.3 (Worked Example: A ball in a box)
